root_cause.text: Memory regions being re-registered with write access (IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS changing from read-only to read-write) were not validated to ensure the underlying user memory (umem) was properly pinned with write permissions, allowing potential unauthorized write access to insufficiently pinned memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces `ib_umem_check_rereg()` function that validates `ib_access_writable(new_access_flags) && !umem->writable` returns an error (-EACCES), preventing the re-registration when transitioning to writable access without proper umem pinning. The CVE description explicitly states "If IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS changes from RO to RW then the umem has to be re-evaluated to ensure it is properly pinned as RW," and the fix references commit b40656aa7d55 ("RDMA/umem: remove FOLL_FORCE usage") which removed forced pinning, exposing this validation gap. The patch mandates all RDMA drivers (mlx4, mlx5, hns, irdma, rxe) call this validation before processing IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation function to prevent unsafe memory region re-registration with incompatible access flags on non-writable umem objects.
intent_record.what: Added a new exported function `ib_umem_check_rereg()` that validates whether a umem object can be re-used during memory region re-registration when only access flags are being changed. The function checks if writable access is being requested on a non-writable umem and returns -EACCES if so.
intent_record.how: This function enables the InfiniBand driver to safely re-use existing umem objects during IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS operations by validating access flag compatibility. It prevents invalid transitions to writable access on read-only umem allocations, which would violate memory protection constraints. The function is exported as a public symbol for use by InfiniBand drivers.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the `irdma_rereg_user_mr()` function which handles memory region re-registration. The vulnerability root cause is that when re-registering with write access (IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS), the code does not validate that the underlying user memory (umem) was properly pinned with write permissions. In the `irdma_rereg_user_mr()` function (lines 3113-3159), when `flags & IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS` is set (line 3138), the code simply updates `iwmr->access = new_access` without any validation that the existing or new umem region supports the requested write access. The function calls `irdma_rereg_mr_trans()` for translation changes (line 3151), which does call `ib_umem_get()` with the access flags (line 3161 in `irdma_rereg_mr_trans`), but when only IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS is set without IB_MR_REREG_TRANS, the code path at line 3152 (`irdma_hwreg_mr()`) is executed without re-acquiring or validating the umem with the new access permissions. The existing umem region is never re-validated or re-pinned to ensure it supports write access when the access flags change from read-only to read-write.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function hns_roce_rereg_user_mr() introduces re-registration support but contains the vulnerable construct. When IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS flag is set (line 1113-1114: 'if (flags & IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS) mr->access = mr_access_flags;'), the function allows changing memory region access flags without validating that the underlying umem is properly pinned with the new access permissions. Specifically, when mr_access_flags changes from read-only to read-write access, the code does not verify that mr->umem was obtained with write permissions. The ib_umem_get() call on line 1088 uses mr_access_flags, but this only occurs when IB_MR_REREG_TRANS flag is set. When only IB_MR_REREG_ACCESS is set (without IB_MR_REREG_TRANS), the existing mr->umem is retained unchanged while mr_access_flags is updated to allow write access (line 1114), creating a mismatch where the memory region claims write access but the underlying pages may not be pinned with write permissions. This violates the security requirement that memory regions must be validated to ensure proper pinning before access permissions are escalated.
